Hi Cathy — thank you for the data. We reviewed usage and sketched a practical conversion path. Attached: proposed_stepup_plan_v1.xlsx (summary + pricing matrix). High level: 

- Committed baseline: convert to a 12-month committed tier at an anchored unit price (price hold for 12 months from effective date).
- Conversion credit: a one-time conversion credit equal to 30% of the first month’s committed spend, amortized across the first 3 billing cycles (appears as monthly bill offset).
- Step-up staircase: auto-step increases every 6 months if rolling 90-day usage > 110% of committed. Each step is +15% of baseline and is priced at the committed unit rate.
- Burst pocket: 20% burst buffer above committed baseline at an overage rate set at 0.75x of on-demand (reduced overage rate to smooth spikes). True-up quarterly.
- Early flexibility: Customers can request immediate step-up once per 12 months without penalty; down-steps are aligned to quarter boundaries.

Action items: Monica/Ben — can you confirm legal/finance OK with amortized credit and the burst overage language? Cathy — if this looks directionally right I'll push a follow-up with the concession matrix and a draft DocuSign wrapper by 11/06.

Best,
